summary: Abandoned, Not Forgotten tells the story of thirteen machines NASA left on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space, by letting each one "write" its own last letter. Instead of a dry list, every machine, from Apollo lunar module descent stages and the Moon buggies to Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Viking, InSight, Ingenuity, Dawn, Pioneer and Kepler, gets a short first-person letter built only from documented facts. Each story also has a live "silence clock" counting the years since its last signal, a "built for / achieved" comparison showing how many times it outlived its plan (Opportunity: about 57 times), and the science it left behind. The project is aimed at school-age space fans, who usually hear about launches but never about how missions end. It matters because these machines are the first monuments beyond Earth: they are heritage, they are still producing science (Apollo laser mirrors still work), and every ending taught engineers something for the next mission, including NASA's return to the Moon.
details:
Abandoned, Not Forgotten is a storytelling project for the challenge "Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars."

What it does: it presents 13 groups of left-behind hardware across three places (the Moon, Mars, and Beyond: asteroid, dwarf planet and deep space). Each has a short first-person "last letter" written from documented facts, a fact list, a live silence clock, a planned-versus-achieved lifetime bar, and ”what it gave us".

How it works: a single self-contained HTML page (interactive cards, a slide-in letter panel, a live clock computed in JavaScript, and an animated chart) plus a 7-slide demo. Illustrations are code-drawn SVG.

Benefits and intended impact: it turns mission endings into stories that young people remember, and shows that "abandoned" does not mean "forgotten": the sites are photographed from orbit, the hardware is protected as heritage, and the lessons shape future missions.

Tools: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, SVG, Python (build scripts), Chrome (PDF export). Creativity: the machines speak for themselves, and the "built for months, worked for years" chart reveals the hidden story of how long they really lasted.
